objects.original: The ambient expression formed from the Laplacian, radial Hessian, radial first derivative and dimension coefficient for arbitrary f and w.
objects.reconstructed: Finite coordinate type I; arbitrary scalar function f on EuclideanSpace R I; point w; ambient Laplacian and first/second Frechet derivatives.

domains.original: Finite coordinate set I, f:ℝ^I→ℝ and w∈ℝ^I. Source DecidableEq I is an unused typing convenience; the compiled definition needs only Fintype I.
domains.reconstructed: I finite (no decidable-equality argument explicitly required); f:R^I→R; w∈R^I.

assumptions.original: I is finite with decidable equality, E is Euclidean space ℝᴵ, f:E→ℝ and w∈E. The subtraction |I|−1 is natural-number subtraction before conversion to ℝ.
assumptions.reconstructed: Assumptions: No unit-norm, smoothness, or nonempty-dimension hypothesis is imposed by the definition.

conclusion.original: For a finite coordinate set I, define the following ambient real-valued expression for every f:ℝᴵ→ℝ and w∈ℝᴵ. On the unit sphere and for a C² ambient test this is the usual extrinsic formula for the sphere Laplacian. Formula: \mathcal L_S f(w)=\Delta f(w)-D^2f(w)[w,w]-(|I|-1)_+Df(w)[w].
conclusion.reconstructed: Conclusion: The defined value is Δf(w)-D²f(w)[w,w]-real(card(I) dotminus 1)·Df(w)[w], where D²f=D(Df), Δ=Laplacian.laplacian, and dotminus is natural-number truncated subtraction performed before coercion to R.

quantifiers.original: This defines a value for every f and every ambient w; it is not a regularity or existence theorem.
quantifiers.reconstructed: Quantifier order: This is a definition giving a real-valued operator at every f and w, not an implication or existence theorem.

scopes.original: Total real-valued definition on all ambient points. Intrinsic sphere interpretation requires restriction to unit points and C² tests. Cardinal subtraction occurs in ℕ before coercion.
scopes.reconstructed: Scope: Defined on the whole ambient Euclidean space, not merely the sphere. Derivatives are Lean's total Frechet derivatives; the definition itself supplies no differential regularity assertion. For card(I)=0 the last coefficient is 0, not -1.

constant_dependencies.original: The coefficient is precisely real(card(I) dotminus 1), so the empty-dimension coefficient is zero.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Constant dependencies: The dimension coefficient is exactly the real coercion of card(I)-1 computed in N.
